identification.summary: Earth Alux is a China-linked cyberespionage group named by Trend Micro. Trend Micro describes it as exploiting vulnerable services on internet-exposed servers, implanting the GODZILLA web shell, and then delivering the VARGEIT and COBEACON backdoors for long-term data collection and exfiltration [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: Trend Micro first saw the group in the second quarter of 2023, mostly in Asia-Pacific; it was also seen in Latin America around mid-2024 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Earth Alux is a Trend Micro cluster name. No Microsoft name or MITRE group ID was found in the sources gathered. The 'China-linked' label is Trend Micro's assessment as relayed by secondary coverage; the primary report page could not be fetched in this session [S1][S2].

attribution.confidence: Trend Micro describes the group as China-linked; no confidence level or state-sponsor identification was found in the sources gathered [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: Trend Micro's own assessment; the cited coverage does not state the specific technical basis for the China link. Not corroborated by any government attribution found [S1][S2].

objectives: Long-term data collection and exfiltration from compromised networks (espionage) [S1][S2].

targeting.notes: Sector list and primary-target countries are as reported in secondary coverage of Trend Micro's report; the list may not be complete [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: Initial access is by exploiting vulnerable services on exposed servers, followed by GODZILLA web shell implantation [S1][S2]. The main backdoor VARGEIT is multi-channel and configurable: it can collect drive information, monitor processes, manipulate files, run command lines and inject further tools, with C2 over HTTP, TCP, UDP, ICMP, DNS and Microsoft Outlook (Graph API and drafts folder), the Outlook channel being the one most often seen [S2]. COBEACON (a Cobalt Strike Beacon) serves mainly as a first-stage backdoor; VARGEIT deploys RAILLOAD (DLL side-loading loader) and RAILSETTER (persistence and timestomping) [S2]. Later MASQLOADER variants can strip security products' NTDLL hooks [S2]. The group was observed testing its tools with Chinese-community open-source utilities ZeroEye and VirTest before deployment [S1][S2]. COBEACON is launched via MASQLOADER or the RSBINJECT shellcode loader; VARGEIT loads tools into a newly started Microsoft Paint process [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: China-linked espionage cluster tracked by Trend Micro; operator identity and sponsor not established in sources [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Web server exploitation, GODZILLA web shell, VARGEIT, COBEACON, RAILLOAD, RAILSETTER, MASQLOADER; pre-deployment tool testing [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Multi-channel C2 including attacker-managed Outlook mailbox via Graph API drafts; Trend Micro's imported summary also cites attacker-controlled cloud storage for exfiltration [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Government, technology, logistics, manufacturing, telecom, IT services and retail in APAC and Latin America [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Internet-exposed servers with vulnerable services; mail platform (Microsoft Outlook/Graph) abused as C2; endpoints with NTDLL-hook-based security tooling [S2].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing web servers and mail infrastructure (Exchange/Outlook cloud mailboxes) in government, telecom and IT-services networks are key terrain [S1][S2]. STEP 2: The actor operates mainly in APAC with expansion to Latin America, relevant to INDOPACOM-adjacent partner networks and contractors [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Template is exposed-service exploitation, GODZILLA web shell, COBEACON/VARGEIT, DLL side-loading and persistence, then collection and exfiltration; C2 hides in legitimate Outlook Graph traffic [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued long-term espionage against APAC government and telecom targets. MDCOA is use of foothold in IT-service or telecom providers to reach downstream customers (not evidenced in sources; hypothesis). Candidate indicators: new web shells on exposed servers, Graph API access to draft messages from servers, DLL side-loading from unusual paths, timestomped files, NTDLL unhooking behavior [S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track inventory and patch status of internet-exposed servers and monitor mail-API (Graph) anomalies. (2) Authorities: hunting on partner or contractor networks requires coordination under existing agreements; no actor-specific authority guidance is supported by sources. (3) Mission assurance: assess dependence on telecom and IT-service providers in APAC theaters. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3/DIB partners and allied CERTs in affected countries [S1][S2].
